consequence_for_pr4: PR 4 (globex_cryptocurrency_tas) is UNAFFECTED and does not need re-examination before it merges. D-8 was raised because the answer could cut either way; it cut the way the ag/crypto gate assumed. The page's 2026-05-29 statement is made once, at page scope, in the opening sentence and again in the page-level “Key Events and Dates” table; the TAS table itself carries no date, so the gate never read a date out of the TAS table — it applied the page's date, which the bytes show is the only way any table on this page is dated. The calibration AGENTS.md requires of an operator's own log is unchanged and still clean: the same page's futures/options table reproduces 26-114 / SER-9740R to the minute, and the page's only exclusion (“Products Not In Scope”) is the twelve spot-quoted futures, which contains no TAS code. PR 4 therefore keeps: the 2026-05-29 one-day bridge and the 2026-05-30 steady state per verdict D3; the sourced order_entry phases per D4; the ECBTC-shaped intersection that withholds the disputed 16:01–16:02 CT minute; and the recorded negative that no filing, SER or notice mentions TAS. One wording fix only: where PR 4 or the ledger says the wiki was “saved 2026-05-22”, it may now also say the version history shows v40 created 2026-05-22T18:58:57Z and no further version until 2026-06-01, so v40 was the live page across the whole cutover, and the TAS table is byte-identical from v39 (2026-05-19) to the current v46 (2026-08-14). consequence_for_crypto_btic: The three crypto BTIC keys move from BLOCKED-ON-U-15 to WRITABLE on the date question. The non-equity BTIC gate's objection — “those are page-revision dates, not effective days” — is correct about the revision log and wrong about where the day lives: the day is not carried by the change log at all, it is carried by the page's opening sentence and by the page-level Key Events row, above and outside every schedule table, with the page's only carve-out naming twelve spot-quoted futures and no BTIC product. The three BTIC tables are h3 siblings of the TAS table under one h2 whose own scope sentence is “schedule impacts for all clients trading cryptocurrency futures and options”, and the same 2026-04-22 revision entry added the TAS table and all three BTIC tables together. So era 2 for globex_cryptocurrency_btic_new_york / _london / _apac is dated by this page at 2026-05-29, on the same warrant and with the same strength as globex_cryptocurrency_tas. FOUR THINGS THIS DOES NOT SETTLE, which must stay on the blocking list for those keys. (1) The page states an INSTANT, not just a day — “Starting at 4 p.m. Central Time on Friday, May 29, 2026” — so under LAW-NO-FABRICATED-DATES the boundary is an exact-instant cutover, and under verdict D3's reasoning the BTIC keys need the same one-day-bridge treatment PR 4 uses (a plain day-level row at 2026-05-29 would rewrite the Thursday-evening leg as a Friday-midnight open). The page's “Day One Extended Maintenance” row is stated for the futures/options books only and gives the BTIC books no day-one reopen, so that one day stays withheld exactly as it is for TAS. (2) The page names no BTIC product code and no BTIC security group anywhere; product membership for the three keys still rests on ContractSpecs and the trading-hours service, not on this page. (3) The source conflict is untouched: the wiki publishes the 16:01–16:02 CT stop for all three BTIC variants and BTC's ContractSpecs omits it, so serve the intersection and record it, as ECBTC and the TAS key do. (4) U-8 verdict N1 is untouched — the London and APAC keys still need a treatment for the weekend block that does not serve a false-closed executable hour across the mismatched DST transitions. Finally, LAW-FOLLOW-UPS-ARE-ISSUES: the plan's row for these keys and decision D-8 must cite a GitHub issue number for each residual that survives (the day-one reopen; the wiki-vs-ContractSpecs minute; N1) before the PR that adds the keys merges.
